audienceTitle: One work profile — whoever you are in the market
audienceSubcopy: Workers and job seekers, freelancers and the self-employed, students and new entrants, career changers, employers, agencies and project owners. Construction is one of many sectors here — not the limit.
pillarsTitle: Your future depends on what the market can actually see
p1Title: Don't let your skills stay invisible
p1Body: A static CV hides most of what you can do. Build a living profile from real, daily activity instead.
p2Body: Show ability across clear levels — self-declared, journal-supported, document-supported, and confirmed — so it reads as proof, not a claim.
p3Title: Built for a market that changes fast
p3Body: The skills employers need keep shifting. A profile that grows with your work keeps you visible as the market moves.
p4Title: Employers shouldn't guess from a weak CV
p4Body: Companies and agencies describe a real need and compare people by evidence, availability, language and country — not a one-page guess.
workerPathBody: Create a profile and describe your skills, experience, documents, preferred country and accommodation needs.
employerPathBody: Tell us what workers or crew you need, where, when, for what jobs and on what terms.
evidenceTitle: The market is changing faster than a CV
evidenceSubcopy: Public statistics from official EU sources on why visible skills, proof and mobility matter. Every card links to its source with a figure date and region.
illustrativeSample: An overview visualisation — it fills as the platform grows.
evidenceDisclaimer: Each claim links to its official public source with the figure date and region. Figures are transcribed from published reports (last verified on the date shown on each card), not a live data feed — always verify against the linked source for the authoritative, latest number.

employment-participation.title: Employment is at a record high — competition for skills is tight
employment-participation.summary: Eurostat reports the EU employment rate for people aged 20–64 reached 75.8% in 2024 — the highest since the series began in 2009 (and rising above 76% in 2025). A tight market makes visible, evidenced skills more valuable, not less.
employment-participation.methodNote: Eurostat Labour Force Survey, EU employment rate age 20–64, 2024 annual (published Apr 2025); highest since the 2009 series start.

shortage-occupations.title: Shortages span the whole labour market
shortage-occupations.summary: The EURES / European Labour Authority report on labour shortages & surpluses lists long-standing shortages in healthcare, construction and hospitality, plus highly-skilled gaps in engineering and IT, and — in the 2024 edition — transport and storage (drivers, mobile-plant operators). The gap is economy-wide, not one sector.
shortage-occupations.methodNote: EURES Report on labour shortages and surpluses 2024; shortage occupations are listed per country at the source.

skills-mismatch.title: Almost half of employers can't find the right skills
skills-mismatch.summary: A European Commission Eurobarometer survey found 46% of EU SMEs found it difficult or very difficult to find staff with the right skills over the past two years — rising to about 70% among SMEs that actually hired. It is a matching problem, not only a supply problem.
skills-mismatch.methodNote: European Commission Eurobarometer on SMEs and skill shortages, 2024: 46% of SMEs found it (very) difficult to find rightly-skilled staff in the prior 24 months; ~70% among SMEs that hired.

digital-skills-demand.title: The skills jobs need are shifting to digital
digital-skills-demand.summary: Cedefop's analysis points to nearly 9 in 10 jobs requiring digital skills, while only about 55.6% of EU adults have at least basic digital skills. The skills profile of many jobs is changing faster than a static CV can show.
digital-skills-demand.unit: % of EU adults with basic digital skills
digital-skills-demand.methodNote: Cedefop, 'Digital skills ambitions in action' / Skills Forecast (2024): ~9/10 jobs will require digital skills; ~55.6% of EU adults have at least basic digital skills.

demographic-pressure.title: The working-age population is shrinking
demographic-pressure.summary: Eurostat population projections show 22 of the 27 EU countries are expected to see their working-age (20–64) population decline by 2050, with the old-age dependency ratio rising substantially. Retaining, re-skilling and matching workers to need becomes structurally more important.
demographic-pressure.unit: EU countries with working-age decline by 2050
demographic-pressure.methodNote: Eurostat population projections / 'Old-age dependency growing across EU regions' (Oct 2025): 22 of 27 EU countries projected to see working-age (20–64) population decline by 2050.

labour-mobility.title: Cross-border mobility helps balance shortages
labour-mobility.summary: The European Commission's Annual Report on Intra-EU Labour Mobility shows about 10.1 million EU citizens of working age work in another member state and roughly 1.83 million are cross-border workers — and movers' employment rate (78%) exceeds nationals' (76%). Relevant for a Baltic & Northern European market where people work across borders.
labour-mobility.methodNote: EC Annual Report on Intra-EU Labour Mobility 2024 (data 2022–2023): ~10.1M working-age EU citizens work abroad; ~1.83M cross-border workers; movers' employment rate 78% vs 76% for nationals.

countryIndexTitle: Source-backed evidence for the markets we serve
countryIndexSubcopy: Baltic & Northern European labour markets. Live pages start with the Baltic core; each figure links to its official source.
countryWorkerFraming: For workers: visible, evidenced skills and mobility matter more where demand is tight.
countryEmployerFraming: For employers: describe the real need and compare people by evidence — not a weak CV.

LT.intro: Lithuania — the home market. Source-backed signals for workers and employers.

shortages.title: Shortages concentrated in trades and operators
shortages.summary: EURES reporting places Lithuania's shortage occupations in stationary plant & machine operators, building and related trades, and food-processing, woodworking and craft trades — alongside the EU-wide gaps in healthcare, IT and transport.

digital-skills.title: Digital skills demand is rising
digital-skills.summary: Cedefop's Skills Forecast points to growing demand for digital and higher-level skills across occupations, including in Lithuania.
